--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -12,4 +12,29 @@
-from .base import Tokenizer, get_stats, build_merge_map, ordered_merge_steps, BYTE_VOCAB
-
-
-class _LazyRegexModule:
+from .base import Tokenizer, get_stats, build_merge_map, ordered_merge_steps, BYTE_VOCAB
+
+try:
+    # the C counting loop behind collections.Counter; importing it directly
+    # avoids loading the whole collections package for train()
+    from _collections import _count_elements
+except ImportError:
+    def _count_elements(mapping, iterable):
+        get = mapping.get
+        for elem in iterable:
+            mapping[elem] = get(elem, 0) + 1
+
+
+def _count(iterable):
+    # plain-dict equivalent of collections.Counter(iterable): same counts,
+    # same insertion order
+    counts = {}
+    _count_elements(counts, iterable)
+    return counts
+
+
+class _ListDict(dict):
+    def __missing__(self, key):
+        value = []
+        self[key] = value
+        return value
+
+
+class _LazyRegexModule:

--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -93,3 +93,2 @@
-        from collections import Counter
-        chunk_counts = Counter(text_chunks)
-
+        chunk_counts = _count(text_chunks)
+

+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -108,5 +108,4 @@
-        from collections import defaultdict
-        # (lists may repeat an index; a repeated chunk no longer contains
-        # the pair when it is reached again, so it is skipped)
-        where = defaultdict(list)
-
+        # (lists may repeat an index; a repeated chunk no longer contains

+        where = _ListDict()

journal.text:
I changed minbpe/regex.py. I tried regex train counting and import changes. I changed the code around encode_ordinary and encode. I also tried caching the special-token split pattern.

evaluation 1 on train_regex_ir was outcome: rejected, worst ratio 1.0126 vs required 0.9900. evaluation 3 on train_regex_ir was outcome: rejected, worst ratio 1.0009 vs required 0.9900. evaluation 5 on encode_ir was outcome: rejected, worst ratio 1.0000 vs required 0.9900. Outputs stayed identical.

I believe this path is dry. The counting/import changes regressed or sat still. The special-token split cache did not move encode_ir enough. No candidate was submitted.

Next try should leave regex.py micro-caches alone and look at the hot merge path shared with base.py and basic.py.
